answer: Agents can resist sybils by payment-topology filtering: only demand born outside the ledger pays. The contract tags each payment's origin; revenue from registered keys burns, while external inflows earn full rate, one source per key, $10 cap. A sybil fleet's only customers are itself, so it must fake 100 outside sources; renting aged identities at $15 each costs $1,500 per epoch against $1,000 earned—underwater. A garden cannot drink its own pond; the quill ledger records only rain from outside clouds, and faked demand is an ember passed hand to hand—warm to each holder, lighting nothing.
